summary: Union County: 1931 24-foot platform tower, replaced in 1933 by a D-6 cupola cab, removed or destroyed in 1959; a 1972 sale may or may not cover the site, and no source describes what remains.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cab (1933), replacing a 24-foot platform tower (1931)
facts.status_note: Cab removed (register) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1959. No source describes what remains at the site.

staffing.status: summer work at the station: a substitute lookout in 1936 and a summer job near the lookout in 1945

access.note: The 1972 sealed-bid offer and August 1972 sale to O. Gordon Hudson may or may not cover this peak. The August notice calls the site the former Medical Springs Lookout Site. No source says whether visitors can reach it now.

events.note: D-6 cupola cabin replaced the platform tower; a Baker newspaper item (September 13, 1933) says it was built under the public works program
J.R. Mitchell went to the Flagstaff lookout station to substitute for Claire Fleetwood, who had been injured
Register says removed in 1959; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959

Former lookout site offered at a sealed-bid sale in July 1972; sold in August 1972 to O. Gordon Hudson of Trail, Oregon, for $789.32. The August notice calls it the former Medical Springs Lookout Site, so the sale may not cover this peak.

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com describe a 24-foot platform tower built in 1931, about 7.3 m. No source gives a height near 207 m. The height of the 1933 cabin is not stated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1959; firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1959. The story reports both and does not choose.

The 1972 notices describe a 4,680-foot mountain and the August notice names the site the former Medical Springs Lookout Site; the register gives 6,511 feet for Flagstaff Butte. The story does not say the sale covered this peak.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains at the site, and the register's 2017 site photo is not described in the text, so it is not cited. The 1972 sale is listed under this site on the Oregon list, but its 4,680-foot mountain does not match the 6,511-foot register elevation, so the editor should decide whether to keep the sale in the record. The brief's height_m of 207.3 looks like an error; the correction proposes 7.3 for the 1931 platform tower only. Staffing evidence is thin (a 1936 substitute and a 1945 summer job near the lookout). The Bulletin item describes the community of Medical Springs, not the lookout. The August 1972 notice names the site the former Medical Springs Lookout Site. The story no longer says the land is private, and the access level is set to unknown for that reason.
